resources.string: Restrictions stay in place until the recovery is completed.

fOCUS helps you set time aside with fewer distractions. You choose a mode, which apps it covers and how long it lasts, and fOCUS shows the exact end time before anything starts.\n\nEverything runs on your device.

Unless your device is set up as a managed device, fOCUS is a normal app. A normal app cannot stop you from force-stopping it, uninstalling it, restarting the phone or entering safe mode, and how calls are handled differs between Android versions and manufacturers.

Whatever your device cannot enforce is shown as unsupported, never as active. fOCUS never blocks emergency calls or emergency information, system recovery, itself or essential system apps.

It is a commitment tool, not an unbreakable lock.

fOCUS has no account and no internet access. Its settings are stored only on this device, and so is anything it stores later, such as session history.\n\nIt shows no permission prompts right now. Android may list a few automatic install-time permissions that let its timer survive a restart. If a feature needs a real permission later, fOCUS explains why when it asks, and the feature stays off if you decline.

fOCUS shows no permission prompts. The one special access it can use is Do Not Disturb access, to silence notifications during a session; you grant it in Android settings and fOCUS never grants it to itself. For its session timer to survive a restart, the background-work library it uses adds a few automatic install-time permissions (such as running after a restart). They are not requested at runtime.

To show your apps it declares which kinds of apps it may see: apps with a launcher icon, and the home, phone, emergency and settings apps so it can protect them. It does not hold Android’s broad permission to see every installed app.

If a later feature needs another, fOCUS explains what it is for and what happens if you decline, at the moment it asks. You can withdraw any permission in Android settings.

Some restrictions can only be enforced on a managed device, where fOCUS is set as the Device Owner. Android typically allows this only during initial device setup, which in practice means after a factory reset that erases the device. fOCUS cannot promote itself, and there is no workaround.\n\nOnly consider this on a device you own and are prepared to reset. fOCUS is designed never to remove emergency calling or system recovery, even on a managed device.

Shizuku lets fOCUS block apps without a factory reset: it runs the system command that pauses an app, with the same rights as a computer connected by USB debugging. Install Shizuku, start it (on Android 11 or newer, through Wireless debugging in Developer options), then allow fOCUS.\n\nShizuku stops when the phone restarts, so start it again before a session. If Shizuku stops during a session, the session keeps running and blocked apps stay blocked; start Shizuku again so fOCUS can check them. If the time runs out while Shizuku is stopped, apps stay blocked until Shizuku runs again. The Shizuku app, settings, phone, emergency and home apps are never blocked, so you can always start Shizuku again.
Shizuku is not running. Install it if you have not, open it, start it, then come back here.
If no dialog appears, open Shizuku, go to authorized apps and allow fOCUS there.

fOCUS blocks apps through Shizuku. Selected apps, Full focus, Call only and Scheduled focus pause apps: they cannot be opened and send no notifications until the session ends. Lock Task is not available this way. fOCUS itself, the home screen, phone, emergency, settings and Shizuku apps are never paused.

This is a regular device. Android does not let a normal app block other apps, so Selected apps, Full focus and Scheduled focus are unsupported here. Call only works in a limited form: it silences notifications except calls, and apps can still be opened.

fOCUS is the Device Owner of this device. Selected apps, Full focus, Call only and Scheduled focus suspend apps: they cannot be opened and send no notifications until the session ends. fOCUS itself, the home screen, phone, emergency and settings apps are never suspended.
Call only on a regular device needs Do Not Disturb access, which only you can grant in Android settings. fOCUS puts your previous Do Not Disturb settings back when the session ends.

Android only allows this on a device with no accounts, typically right after a factory reset and before setup is finished. With USB debugging enabled and fOCUS installed, run on a computer:

adb shell dpm set-device-owner com.focus.app/.device.FocusDeviceAdminReceiver

If Android refuses, the device is not eligible and fOCUS stays a regular app. Behavior can differ between Android versions and manufacturers; fOCUS only reports what the device confirms.

fOCUS works entirely on your device. It has no account, no internet permission and no analytics. Nothing is sent anywhere. The list of apps you select, your session history, the trusted person’s name (and optional phone number), a salted hash of their PIN and the recovery log are stored only on this device.\n\nStatistics are calculated on the device from that history and add nothing to what is stored. To delete everything it stores, clear its storage in Android settings or uninstall it.
fOCUS never promises an unbreakable lock. On a regular device it cannot prevent force-stop, uninstall, restart or safe mode.

If you or someone else is in danger, call your local emergency number now.\n\nfOCUS never blocks emergency calling or emergency information. This screen needs no PIN, has no waiting time and is not recorded anywhere.
This opens your phone app with 112 entered, a number most phones treat as an emergency number. You press call yourself. If your local emergency number is different, dial that one.
This device has no app that can open that.

Calling does not end the session, and it does not need to: the phone, home and settings apps stay available while it runs.\n\nIf the restrictions must be lifted, your trusted person can end the session with their PIN.
End session with a trusted person
fOCUS does not place calls itself and holds no call permission. Nothing about this screen is stored or sent.
Who can end a session early, and how
No trusted person is set up, so this session ends only when its time is up. Emergency calling stays available.
%1$s can end this session early with their PIN. Emergency calling always stays available.
No trusted person with a PIN is set up. Once started, this session can only end when its time is up. Emergency calling stays available.
fOCUS cannot read its trusted-person data right now. If you start, assume the session can only end when its time is up. Emergency calling stays available.

A trusted person is someone you choose, such as a family member or a friend, who can end a session early. fOCUS never contacts them: it has no internet permission and sends nothing anywhere.

How it works: you hand them the phone once, and they choose a secret PIN and type it in. Only a salted hash of the PIN is kept on this device, so fOCUS cannot show it to you. To end a session early, they must enter it on this phone. Each PIN works once; after it was used, they choose a new one.

What it can do: end the running session and lift its restrictions. What it cannot do: it does not remove Device Owner status or the app, and it does not cancel scheduled sessions for later days. Emergency calling never needs it.

While a session is running, nothing here can be changed. Too many wrong PINs lock the PIN entry for a growing time. If the PIN is forgotten, you can ask to remove the trusted person; that becomes possible 24 hours later, only when no session is running.
A session is running. Trusted-person settings cannot be changed until it ends.
fOCUS cannot read the trusted-person data on this device. Nothing was changed. Until it can be read, assume a session can only end when its time is up.
The PIN was used to end a session. A new PIN is needed before this person can end another one.
Enter the current PIN to remove the trusted person. Afterwards, sessions can only end when their time is up.

You can ask to remove the trusted person without the PIN. It becomes possible 24 hours after the request, only while no session is running, and you can cancel the request. Nothing is hidden: the request is recorded in the recovery log.
